body.statement: For every \(N\), \(\inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}P_X^N\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N\}\ge1-\alpha\). On the simultaneous covariance event, \(\operatorname{ex}(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))\le4L_\beta\Delta_N\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P_X\in\mathcal M\), and, for \(J\in\mathcal J\), put \(S_J=D\cup J\).  We first establish the branchwise bounds used below.  Let \(H,H'\) be positive-definite matrices with spectra contained in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), and write \(\delta=\lVert H-H'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  If \(Y\in S_J\), then the definition of partial covariance gives
\[
 \gamma_{YT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)
 =H_{YT}-H_{YS_J}H_{S_JS_J}^{-1}H_{S_JT}=0,
\]
because \(H_{YS_J}H_{S_JS_J}^{-1}\) is the coordinate row selecting \(Y\) from \(S_J\).  Also \(T\notin S_J\): every member of \(D\) strictly precedes \(T\), whereas every member of \(J\) is incomparable with \(T\).  Thus \(\gamma_{TT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)>0\), because it is the Schur complement of the positive-definite principal block \(H_{S_JS_J}\).  Hence \(\beta_J(H)=0\).  The same argument applies to \(H'\).

Suppose next that \(Y\notin S_J\), and set \(B_J=S_J\cup\{T\}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:distinct\text{-}targets}\) implies \(Y\notin B_J\).  Block Gaussian elimination, applied to the partition \(B_J=S_J\cup\{T\}\), gives the partial-regression identity
\[
 \beta_J(H)=e_T^{\mathsf T}H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}H_{B_JY}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, eliminating the coordinates in \(S_J\) from the normal equations for the regression of coordinate \(Y\) on coordinates \(B_J\) leaves the coefficient of coordinate \(T\) equal to \(\gamma_{YT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)/\gamma_{TT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)\), whose denominator is positive by the same Schur-complement argument.

Every principal submatrix of \(H\) and \(H'\) has smallest eigenvalue at least \(\lambda\), by \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}lower}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}upper}\) also gives \(\lVert H_{B_JY}\rVert_2\le\Lambda\) and \(\lVert H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2\le\Lambda\), since each is a coordinate restriction of \(He_Y\) or \(H'e_Y\).  Consequently, (1) implies
\[
 |\beta_J(H)|
 \le \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H_{B_JY}\rVert_2
 \le \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, the inverse identity
\[
 H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}-(H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}
 =H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}
   \bigl(H'_{B_JB_J}-H_{B_JB_J}\bigr)
   (H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}
\]
and contraction of the operator norm under coordinate restriction yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\beta_J(H)-\beta_J(H')|
 &\le \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H_{B_JY}-H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2 \\
 &\quad+
       \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}-(H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2 \\
 &\le \left(\lambda^{-1}+\Lambda\lambda^{-2}\right)\delta
 =L_\beta\delta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
When \(Y\in S_J\), both coefficients are zero, so (2)--(3) remain valid.  We have therefore proved, for every \(J\in\mathcal J\),
\[
 |\beta_J(H)|\le\frac{\Lambda}{\lambda},
 \qquad
 |\beta_J(H)-\beta_J(H')|
 \le L_\beta\lVert H-H'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{4}
\]
This label-preserving estimate also proves directly the pointwise ingredient behind \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\text{-}lipschitz}\), without requiring distinct values among the ideal branches.

On the fallback branch of \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\), membership of \(P_X\) in \(\mathcal M\), together with \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}lower}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}upper}\), permits (4) with \(H=\Gamma\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) and the fallback clause of \(\mathrm{def:fiber\text{-}region}\) then give
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)
 =\{\beta_J(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}
 \subseteq[-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]
 =C_N.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus coverage is certain on that deterministic branch.

Now suppose that the active-branch conditions \(t_N\ge1\) and \(m_N\ge2\varepsilon_N\) hold.  Let \(\mathcal E_N\) be the simultaneous event supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:fourier\text{-}region}\).  On this event,
\[
 \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\Delta_N,
\tag{6}
\]
and, by that theorem and \(\mathrm{ass:iid}\),
\[
 \inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}P_X^N(\mathcal E_N)\ge1-\alpha_N.
\tag{7}
\]
Spectral clipping in \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\) places the spectrum of \(\widehat\Gamma_N\) in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), and the spectral assumptions do the same for \(\Gamma\).  Applying (4) to (6) therefore gives, simultaneously for every \(J\in\mathcal J\),
\[
 |\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)-\beta_J(\Gamma)|
 \le2L_\beta\Delta_N.
\tag{8}
\]
By (4), \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\) also belongs to the fixed clipping interval \([ -\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\).  Thus (8) puts \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\) in the corresponding clipped interval appearing in \(C_N\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) now implies, on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(\alpha_N=\min\{\alpha,(N+1)^{-2}\}\le\alpha\), equations (5), (7), and (9) show, for every \(N\),
\[
 \inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 P_X^N\!\left\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha_N\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{10}
\]

It remains to prove the asserted directed-excess bound on the active-branch simultaneous covariance event.  Take \(x\in C_N\).  Since \(\mathcal J\) is finite, the definition of \(C_N\) gives some \(J\in\mathcal J\) for which
\[
 |x-\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)|\le2L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
The exact representation in \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) gives \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\).  Hence (8) and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)}|x-\theta|
 \le |x-\beta_J(\Gamma)|
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(x\in C_N\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{ex}\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right)
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N.
\tag{11}
\]
The argument never selects a linear extension and never divides by a difference between two effect values.  The only divisions are by Schur complements bounded away from zero through the spectral lower bound.  Consequently (8)--(11) continue to hold on exact effect-collision strata.

Finally, measurability of the covariance construction is part of \(\mathrm{thm:fourier\text{-}region}\).  Each map \(H\mapsto\beta_J(H)\) is continuous on the spectrally bounded positive-definite set by (1), matrix inversion being continuous there.  The family \(\mathcal J\) is finite because \(V\) is finite.  Therefore the finite union of clipped closed intervals defining \(C_N\) is a measurable nonempty compact random set on the active branch; it is plainly so on the fallback branch.  Thus all events and directed excesses used above are measurable.
body.justification: The theorem supplies finite-sample simultaneous coverage of the complete mixed-noise effect fiber, rather than asymptotic coverage of one effect after order-confidence and adjustment-set steps.
body.gap: Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 work in a causally sufficient recursive additive-error model with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and order identifiability from nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors; their effect interval is asymptotically valid for one total effect conditional on order-set and adjustment-interval validity. The present model instead permits latent common sources, identifies a greatest Gaussian divisor by Fourier tails, and gives finite-sample simultaneous inclusion of every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect; no blanket inclusion relation between the two full model classes is asserted.
body.consumer: The \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) workflow can report a confidence-enlarged set of all compatible effects rather than a selected list.
